title: Seller gap-mapping competitive play — atelier (draft)
summary: Working draft deck for a new seller-facing play that maps customer gaps vs. competitors and prescribes tactical seller moves (technical pairing, cost/latency demos, fallback choreography). Purpose: shorten cycles on mid-market pilots and surface win signals for platform accounts.
slides:
Slide 1 — Title: Seller Gap-Mapping Competitive Play (Atelier) — Draft
Speaker note: quick sync before Q2 enablement. Not a polished deck — this is an atelier: play experiments + scripts for SEs and sellers.

Slide 2 — Goal + success criteria:
- Primary goal: Reduce pilot time-to-decision by 30% for platform/prod teams
- Success metrics: pilot conversion rate, time-to-first-meaningful-throughput, escrowed fallback tests run
Speaker note: tie to SDR/SE KPIs and pilot OKRs.

Slide 3 — When to use this play:
- Customer evaluating Redwood vs. managed LLM cloud or competitor on dedicated/private path
- Pilot stalls on cost predictability, latency spikes, or rollback concerns
- Technical buyer needs guarded fallback story and routing assurance
Speaker note: use after initial POC shows model quality parity but ops questions persist.

Slide 4 — Buyer personas + what they care about:
- Integration Architect: deterministic latency, routing, rollout controls
- Platform Engineer: autoscaling, reserved capacity economics
- Product Manager: inference quality & UX latency budgets
- Security/Compliance: private deployment options, auditability
Speaker note: map objections to persona.

Slide 5 — Gap mapping framework (stitch & salvage):
- Column A: Customer pain (e.g., token cost surprise)
- Column B: Competitor promise (e.g., lowest per-token price)
- Column C: Redwood counter (e.g., caching + quantization pilot, routing policy)
- Column D: Tactical seller move (demo, benchmark, JIT config)
Speaker note: keep this at 1-slide in calls; follow with technical appendix if requested.

Slide 6 — Common gaps and our choreography (examples):
- Cost predictability gap -> Redwood move: reserved capacity pilot + cost projection sheet; seller move: run 3-day synthetic with burst profile
- Latency outlier gap -> Redwood move: fallback routing + KV caching; seller move: live trace demo, show console alerts
- Model regression fear -> Redwood move: evals + canary rollouts; seller move: provide promptset regressions and rollback plan
Speaker note: include URLs to demo scripts in follow-up email.

Slide 7 — Demo playbooks (ops + seller):
- Micro-demo: 8-minute Jupyter with synthetic traffic showing cache hit rate and 40% token reduction
- Failover demo: orchestrated region outage and automatic fallback to warm variants
- Cost projection: spreadsheet scenario builder for 3 workload shapes
Speaker note: attach links to notebooks and spreadsheet templates in the follow-up.

Slide 8 — SE pairing checklist (pre-call):
- Confirm traffic shape and p95 latency SLA target
- Collect sample promptset and average sequence length
- Confirm security requirements (VPC/KMS) and data residency needs
- Prepare two competitor claims to rebut with benchmarks
Speaker note: checklist to paste in calendar invite 1 hour before demo.

Slide 9 — Seller script (30–90s snippets):
- Discovery opener: 'Tell me about the times latency causes the team to degrade the user experience...'
- Reassurance line: 'We treat model quality as immutable — routing and caching are how we get predictable economics.'
- Close prompt: 'Would you be open to a 72-hour reserved-capacity pilot that demonstrates both cost and stability guarantees?'
Speaker note: practice these with peer roleplay.

Slide 10 — Evidence pack (what to send after call):
- Short report: 72-hour pilot plan + expected cost delta
- Notebook: cache + quantization test with sample results
- Rollout plan: canary steps and observability checklist
- Legal checkpoint: brief on data handling for Private deployments
Speaker note: email template in appendix.

Slide 11 — Risks, mitigation, and escalation ladder:
- Risk: pilot shows model quality degradation after quantization
  Mitigation: fall back to full precision variant, auto-rollout, and compare evals
- Risk: customer wants single-region SLAs we can't meet initially
  Mitigation: propose staged SLA with fallback routing and credits for breach
- Escalation: include SRE on call if an ops test is scheduled
Speaker note: attach incident runbook snippet for sellers.

Slide 12 — Metrics to track during pilot:
- Conversion indicators: number of integration touchpoints, demo repeat requests
- Technical signals: median latency, p95 tail, cache hit ratio, tokens per session
- Business signals: projected monthly spend variance, estimated unit cost delta
Speaker note: set a dashboard template for the customer and share read-only link.

Slide 13 — Next steps and owner roles:
- SE: run baseline synthetic and produce the cost projection (owner: SE)
- Seller: lock pilot contract and procurement questions (owner: AE)
- Solutions Eng: run failover demo and attach logs (owner: Solutions Eng)
- Customer Success: prepare onboarding checklist day 1 (owner: CS)
Speaker note: propose a 2-week cadence with weekly checkpoints.

Slide 14 — Appendix: email template and quick links:
- Quick follow-up email template (short, includes 3 links: pilot plan, notebook, spreadsheet)
- Links: Confluence evidence page, demo repo, pilot SOW template
Speaker note: copy-paste ready templates live in Confluence linked above.

Slide 15 — Open questions for the atelier:
- Which competitor claims are surfacing most in EMEA mid-market accounts?
- Can we standardize a 72-hour reserved pilot SKU for mid-market?
- Which demo assets need automation to be run on-demand by SEs?
Speaker note: capture answers and iterate on next version.

Slide 16 — Action items (owner + due date):
- Miguel: create notebook runner that accepts sample promptset (due: 2026-03-17)
- Claire: draft Pilot SOW template for reserved capacity (due: 2026-03-21)
- Ravi: produce 3 competitor one-pagers with rebut lines (due: 2026-03-22)
- Aisha: run two roleplays and collect feedback (due: 2026-03-24)
Speaker note: track in JIRA-1245.

Slide 17 — Minimal legal notes (for quick checks):
- Private deployment exceptions: standard NDA + addendum for HSM/KMS requirements
- Data residency: confirm region and retention window in SOW
Speaker note: escalate to Legal for any non-standard asks.

Slide 18 — Closing: how this play shortens cycles
- By mapping concrete gaps to demoable remedies, sellers can convert hesitancy into a measurable pilot with success criteria and rollback paths
- Expected outcome: faster approvals, clearer procurement asks, and fewer stalled pilots
Speaker note: ask for volunteers to run pilot with early customers.
